lessons.title: Fix a lost reservation
lessons.objective: Show your reservation confirmation, ask what the restaurant can offer, and accept or decline an alternative table.
lessons.focus: Use 「〜の名前で予約しています」 to give the booking name, 「こちらが〜です」 to present the confirmation, and 「〜ていただけますか」 to ask politely what seating is available.
lessons.scene: You arrive at 8 for your anniversary, but the host cannot find your reservation. You say it is under the name Miller and open your email to show the confirmation. The host sees the confirmation number, apologizes for the mistake, and offers a table on the terrace now or a table inside in 30 minutes. You don't want to wait, so you accept the terrace table.

lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: learn what diners wear, whether jackets are required, and what smart casual means locally
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: Call the restaurant to ask whether shorts are acceptable and what diners usually wear.
lessons.title: Ask about the dress code
lessons.objective: Ask whether the restaurant has a dress code, what smart casual means there, whether a jacket is required, whether shorts are allowed, and what guests usually wear to dinner.
lessons.focus: Ask what smart casual means at this restaurant and whether jackets or shorts are allowed. 着る is used for tops; 履く is used for pants and shoes.
lessons.scene: The guest calls the restaurant about tonight's reservation to ask about the dress code. The receptionist says that the dining room asks for smart casual. The guest asks what that means, and the receptionist explains that most guests wear a collared shirt and long pants, but a jacket is not required. The guest asks whether shorts are allowed. The receptionist says not in the dining room, but yes on the terrace, and sandals are fine too. The guest decides to wear long pants and closed-toe shoes.

lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: ask about early seatings, a children's menu, and what the kitchen can adapt
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: Ask whether a 7 p.m. table works with two tired children and what the kitchen can make for them.
lessons.title: Bring children to dinner
lessons.objective: Ask for a 7 p.m. table for two adults and two children, ask about the first seating, a children's menu, and what the kitchen can adapt, and tell the restaurant about a nut allergy.
lessons.focus: Asking for a 7 p.m. table for a family, asking about the first seating and a children's menu, asking for a small portion and sauce on the side, requesting a high chair, and stating a nut allergy.
lessons.scene: A guest calls a downtown restaurant to make a reservation for the family. The waiter says the first seating at 7 is quieter and that the restaurant has no children's menu, but the kitchen can make small portions. The guest asks for the sauce on the side, and the waiter agrees and says a high chair will be brought for the little girl. The guest says the daughter is allergic to nuts and asks the waiter to tell the chef.
